title: Assurance Control Mapping and Sensitive Evidence Boundary

preflight.note: Created before assurance-mapping schema/template, sensitive-evidence validation, framework-drift, or claim-safety implementation begins.

acceptance_criteria.text: Define a provider-neutral assurance/control mapping record or extension model that can express framework/version/source authority, requirement identifier, applicability status and rationale, adopter control/invariant/policy owner, implementation references, evidence references, responsibilities, third-party dependencies, gaps/exceptions, review freshness, and any independent attestation reference.

The model makes implemented control, evidence that a control operated, framework mapping, applicability conclusion, and independent audit/certification distinct states; RepoPact never infers legal compliance or certification from control/evidence presence.

Define and validate a sensitive-evidence boundary that prefers hashes, counts, redacted/synthetic fixtures, bounded metadata, run identifiers, controlled external references, and non-secret configuration snapshots over raw regulated/customer payloads in Git evidence.

Add guardrails or validator guidance sufficient to flag obvious evidence-policy violations involving secrets, credentials, PHI/health records, cardholder data, passports/financial identity, or equivalent restricted payloads without pretending pattern matching can fully classify all sensitive data.

Use RepoPact provenance/review semantics to surface stale framework mappings, stale control review, evidence/source drift, implementation changes that invalidate mappings, and documentation claims stronger than the stored evidence supports.

Framework content and legal interpretations remain adopter-owned inputs/extensions rather than hard-coded SOC 2, HIPAA, PCI DSS, GDPR, KYC/AML, FERPA, COPPA, FDA, or other jurisdiction-specific conclusions in the RepoPact kernel.

Provide a conformance/example path using the ForgeWire assurance program as one adopter while proving the feature remains generic and optional for repositories with no regulated/compliance mapping needs.
